articles.title: Eavesdropping on Silence: How Submarine Internet Cables Can Now Detect Whales Without a Sound
articles.summary: Most whale tracking relies on their deafening calls, but what about when they go quiet? Norwegian researchers have tapped into undersea fiber-optic cables to detect the subtle pressure waves whales create just by swimming. This breakthrough could fill a massive blind spot in marine conservation.

articles.title: AI's '7' Problem: How Large Language Models Got Stuck in a Groupthink Groove
articles.summary: Ask any major chatbot for a random number, and you'll probably get 7. This eerie predictability exposes a deeper flaw: LLMs converge on the same clichéd answers. Startup Springboards built Flint, a model designed to break the mold and serve up genuine variety for creative tasks.

articles.title: Turning Grid Bottlenecks into Bargains: How Surplus Renewable Power Could Slash Green Hydrogen Costs
articles.summary: When renewable energy overwhelms the grid, operators often curtail it—wasting clean electricity. German researchers show that using this excess power for hydrogen production can cut costs by up to €1.96 per kg, but only if the surplus electricity is nearly free and combined with steadier sources.
